title: Colts-Texans preview with Jonathan Alexander; Can Indy avoid 0-3 hole?
text: The Athletic's James Boyd and the Houston Chronicle's Jonathan Alexander preview the Indianapolis Colts' upcoming home game against the Houston Texans. The winless Colts have lost five straight against the also winlessTexans. Can Indy finally snap that streak to potentially save its season? Hosted by Simplecast, an AdsWizz company. title: How do the Broncos and Bo Nix build the PERFECT gameplan to beat the Rams? | Orange & Blue Today
text: It’s a Friday GamePlan edition of Orange & Blue Today, and Cecil & Mase lay out exactly how the Broncos can beat the Rams on Sunday Night Football in Week 3 — a matchup that demands discipline, creativity, and a smart approach on both sides of the ball. On offense, the big question is the running back rotation. JK Dobbins is working through a hamstring injury — will he be close to full strength by Sunday. If he is, how should Denver attack on the ground. And if he’s limited, how much of the load shifts to RJ Harvey, whose burst and space ability could create chunk plays against the Rams’ front. In the passing game, Jaylen Waddle dominated targets last week. Does that continue, or does Bo Nix spread the ball around more. And how does Nix’s growing chemistry with Davis Webb — especially Webb’s clarity and communication — shape the gameplan under the prime‑time spotlight. Defensively, the challenge is clear: Matthew Stafford, Terrance Ferguson, and Davante Adams form one of the most dangerous passing attacks in football. How does Denver disrupt timing, disguise coverage, and keep Stafford from getting comfortable. 🔥 In this episode: How the Broncos should attack with JK Dobbins Why RJ Harvey could be a big‑play threat vs the Rams What Jonah Coleman’s injury means for the rotation How Bo Nix distributes targets — and Waddle’s role How Denver slows Stafford, Ferguson, and Davante Adams Drop your thoughts — what’s the biggest key for Denver to beat the Rams on Sunday night.

text: Joining us right now, Jeff Legwald, ESPN. Let's preview this Broncos-Rams matchup. Jeff, let's start with the Bronco injury report. No Jonah Coleman, but full participation for two days out of J.K. Dobbins and R.J. Harvey. How healthy do we think these guys are? The Jonah Coleman situation was a little... odd in that he was on the field in uniform uh every day during the the open time when we're out there and often especially when a guy has a leg injury uh you know they're they're kept off their feet or inside getting treatment so that that was a little strange but you know and he would go through stretching and some of the light moving around but yeah that the fact he was listed as a did not participate all week and won't play Sunday unless there's some kind of significant miracle improvement where he gets upgraded. So that was a little odd, but the other two guys are ready to go. They didn't even give him a game designation, which means they're 100% and will play as scheduled. So you don't think they'll call up any, they won't use any call-ups on trade or anybody else. Then we would feel like we're safe to go with those three. But Andy, you don't, I mean, they've used their two call-ups for, they don't have a long snapper. So he has to be called up unless they move them to the roster, uh, between now and tomorrow. Uh, so they use the two call-ups the previous two weeks on a fullback, Adam Prentice and a long snapper, uh, The long snapper would have to be one of those. And, you know, I asked him today, would you call somebody up? And his answer was basically, I don't want to tell you, but I think we're okay, was kind of how he put it. So I would still think it's Prentice and Furboni as the call-ups there with Prentice maybe to carry the ball in short yardage if he asked to. Leggy, what have you seen, speaking of offensive pieces that are available for this team, and, you know, we're talking about Adam Prentice and, you know, Broncos used some 22 last week. What have you seen out of this team as you've charted the Broncos through two weeks formationally, you know, going heavier and what Jalen Waddell has opened up in this offense? Give us a breakdown of kind of how Sean Payton and Davis Webb are using the personnel they have this year. Well, Nate, I think this game especially, The Rams very much like to live in the nickel and the dime if you let them get away with it. So I would expect the Broncos to try and force the issue from time to time with multiple tight ends, multiple backs and heavier looks. So I think they felt better about how things went, you know, obviously against Jacksonville when they were, heavier at times and they were more committed to the run and Bo Nix was under center more. So I think, you know, they will lean that way against these kinds of defenses or, you know, if they don't, that would be a little, a little quizzical, but I think given that the Rams like to play, if you let them in the lighter looks on defense, that the Broncos will try and force the issue and go the other way. Jeff, you know, it was interesting because I feel like, you know, Nate was breaking down some of the snaps that everybody played and how it's been affecting everybody. And one of the ones that he came up with, again, was you said, right, Nate, because of the tight end use, especially out of the first, I guess, in last week's game, Jadé Barron not playing a lot last week. What do you think's going on with Jadé there? Again, is it just because of formations? Is he taking a step back or is it just still be patient? If somebody goes down, he's going to play a big role. Well, you know, Andy, that's one of those things where, you know, personnel, I mean, sometimes on defense you can just say, look, we're just playing this and we don't care. But Jacksonville, you know, essentially forced the issue. Teams don't want to face the Broncos' pass rush out of the nickel and the dime. So Jacksonville stayed really heavy. So you're, you know, that other corner isn't going to play any snaps if they won't come out of those heavier looks. And that's why he didn't get much and, you know, against the Jags. And I think, you know, until, you know, there's some movie, you know, you got guys who are free agents next March, but as long as Riley Moss and Jaquan McMillan and Sertan are healthy, you know, Barron is, is in that dime role and they have to be in the dime, you know, for him to be out there in some of the bigger nickel things. And if, and if they don't get a look from the offense to use him, you know, that's just how it's going to be this year has no bearing on what they think of him as a player. They, they, they actually believe he had one of the best off seasons training camps of anybody in On the defense, so it's not a question of ability or what's going on with the first rounder. Riley Moss is a really good corner. Jaquan McMillan is one of the best nickels in the league. There's just not room for him right now unless they go to the dime. That's Jeff Legwald of ESPN. Great breakdown right there, Leggy. We're live at Old Town Tavern in Arvada. Bud Light football Friday. Great specials on Bud Light right now. Leggy, we have got two A-plus heavyweight matchups in this game, receivers versus corners. On one end, Devontae Adams going up against PS2. On the other, Jalen Waddell going up against Trent McDuffie. Jeff, give us the breakdown on both of these matchups because this is some really, really good head-to-head football we're about to watch on Sunday night. Yeah, this is kind of a football geek like I am. These are the things that are fun to chart and break down and see happen in real time. Devontae Adams' superpower is the first yard and a half of the route. There are some guys who are pretty good at getting a release at the line of scrimmage. He is He's at the pinnacle, even at this age and this experience level. His release is still among the best in the league, and he leaves plenty of people flailing in his wake. Watching this past week when they were trying to line up rookies and young corners against him in man-press situations, that didn't go well. And that's why the numbers look the way it did. You know, Sertan's a totally different thing. You know, a lot of people have made Adams' numbers against Sertan or whatever. You know, most of that was the first meeting. Since then, it's been a really good fight. And Sertan's at the top of his game. I just told somebody today, I was talking to a scout in the league, and Sertan had two snaps against the Jags that were– absolutely perfect teaching tape kind of snaps on plays he made on the ball against the Jaguars just mirroring routes that other people can't do so that I would expect them especially if Nakua is not going to play to get Sertan on Adams a lot and take their chances with everybody else and mix it up and match a little bit But I think that is a matchup we'll actually see. Now, you know, will the Rams answer that way with Waddle? I mean, it's, you know, Sutton is a problem if you don't have a plan. If you match McDuffie, that leaves a very physical, good boundary receiver in Sutton, you know, working the edges of formation. And, but I would expect them to, you know, they didn't sign McDuffie not to use them in situations like this, but it's hard to match waddle through the middle of the field, just in man to man. But again, the flip side to it, and to your point there, Jeff, is teams want to zone Bo Nix up as much as they possibly can because if you go into man... You simply play into his hands. So they, they want the reaction to Waddle. Thanks, dude. Thanks, fellas. We'll see you.
